```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,

```

# Purpose

Every step-4 document so far has fitted IgG and IgM **separately** --- four
methods, eight independent models, no term connecting them. That design cannot
answer one question people keep asking of it: *does the DS effect differ between
the two isotypes?* The concordance scatterplots put two separately-fitted
coefficient sets on the same axes, which is descriptive. It is not a test.

This document fits a **single model over both isotypes at once** and asks the
question directly. Two models, same cells, same genes, same random effect:

$$\textbf{additive:}\quad \sim t + g + s + c + (1\,|\,\text{donor})$$
$$\textbf{interaction:}\quad \sim t + g \times s + c + (1\,|\,\text{donor})$$

with $t$ processing time, $g$ study group, $s$ isotype, $c$ the cellular
detection rate. The interaction coefficient is tested by likelihood-ratio test,
which **is** the comparison between the two models --- a gene with no interaction
is a gene for which the additive model is sufficient.

**Reading the coefficients.** `isotype` is coded with IgG as the reference, so in
the interaction model `studyGroupDS` is *the DS effect within IgG*, not a main
effect averaged over both. The DS effect within IgM is
`studyGroupDS + studyGroupDS:isotypeIGHM`. All three are reported below. In the
additive model `studyGroupDS` is a single DS effect constrained to be the same in
both isotypes.

**What counts as evidence.** Three things, in order of how much weight they
carry:

1. the number of genes whose interaction clears FDR, against what the permutation
   null produces;
2. the shape of the interaction p-value histogram --- flat means no interaction
   anywhere, a spike near zero means some genes genuinely differ;
3. whether the additive model's DS effect agrees with the two per-isotype effects
   estimated separately in `P635_step4_DE_mast.Rmd`.

Given that every per-isotype analysis returned no differentially expressed genes,
the prior here is firmly that there is nothing to find. The point of the exercise
is to be able to say so from a model that was actually capable of finding it.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(knitr)
library(MAST)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(lme4)
library(patchwork)
library(limma)
library(msigdbr)
```

# Parameters

```{r params}
STEP3_RDS <- file.path("pseudobulk_clean_output", "step3_cells_time_structure.rds")
OUT_DIR   <- "pseudobulk_clean_output"
FIG_DIR   <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures", "mast_combined")
SRC_DIR   <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figure_source_data", "mast_combined")
CACHE_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "cache", "mast_combined")

DE_ISOTYPES <- c("IGHG", "IGHM")

## Donor inclusion matches the per-isotype documents: a donor contributes its
## cells of an isotype only if it has at least MIN_CELLS of them. A donor can
## therefore contribute IgG cells but not IgM. The gene filter, by contrast, is
## recomputed on the pooled matrix, since that is the matrix being modelled.
MIN_CELLS   <- 5
CELL_DETECT <- 0.10

FORMULA_ADD <- ~ TimeElapsed_binary + studyGroup + isotype + cngeneson + (1 | donorId)
FORMULA_INT <- ~ TimeElapsed_binary + studyGroup * isotype + cngeneson + (1 | donorId)
COEF_GROUP  <- "studyGroupDS"                 # DS effect (in IgG, under FORMULA_INT)
COEF_INT    <- "studyGroupDS:isotypeIGHM"     # how that effect shifts in IgM

FDR     <- 0.10
LFC_MIN <- 1
N_LABELS <- 12

## Permutation null for the interaction test. Group labels are shuffled between
## donors and every cell carries its donor's new label, so donor structure,
## isotype assignment and cells-per-donor are all untouched -- only the
## DS/control contrast is randomised. Under that null there is no group effect
## and therefore no interaction either, so the number of genes the interaction
## test calls is a direct read on its calibration.
RUN_PERM <- TRUE
## Split deliberately. The interaction permutation confirms a null that three
## independent lines already establish (0 genes, flat p-value histogram, flat
## interaction GSEA), so it is kept cheap. The group permutation is the one that
## decides whether the called genes are real, and gets the full count: with 50
## the empirical p can reach 1/51 = 0.02, against 1/11 = 0.09 at ten.
N_PERM_INT   <- 10
N_PERM_GROUP <- 50

GSEA_COLLECTION <- "H"
GSEA_MIN_SIZE   <- 10
GSEA_MAX_SIZE   <- 500
## 0.10, matching the gene-level FDR used throughout this project. The dashed
## line on the hallmark figure and the bar colouring both read from this, so they
## cannot drift apart. Note the consequence: at 0.10 one set (KRAS_SIGNALING_DN,
## FDR 0.093) is called, where at 0.05 nothing was.
GSEA_FDR        <- 0.10
GSEA_N_SHOW     <- 10

SEED    <- 42
N_CORES <- max(1L, min(8L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L))
options(mc.cores = N_CORES)
USE_CACHE <- TRUE

for (d in c(OUT_DIR, FIG_DIR, SRC_DIR, CACHE_DIR))
  dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

cached <- function(name, key, expr) {
  path <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, sprintf("%s.rds", name))
  if (USE_CACHE && file.exists(path)) {
    obj <- readRDS(path)
    if (identical(obj$key, key)) { cat(sprintf("cache hit: %s\n", basename(path))); return(obj$value) }
  }
  t0 <- Sys.time(); value <- expr
  saveRDS(list(key = key, value = value), path)
  cat(sprintf("computed %s in %.1f min\n", basename(path),
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
  value
}
saveSource <- function(dat, name, description) {
  path <- file.path(SRC_DIR, sprintf("%s.csv", name))
  write_csv(dat, path)
  cat(sprintf("source data: %-46s %5d rows  (%s)\n", basename(path), nrow(dat), description))
  invisible(path)
}
savePanel <- function(plot, name, width = 6.5, height = 4.5) {
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s.pdf", name)), plot, width = width, height = height)
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s.png", name)), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  invisible(plot)
}
```

# Load step 3 and pool the isotypes

```{r load_step3}
step3     <- readRDS(STEP3_RDS)
rawCounts <- step3$counts
cells     <- step3$cellAnno
geneAnno  <- step3$geneAnno
stopifnot(all(rawCounts %% 1 == 0))

IG_PATTERN <- "^IG[HKL](V|D|J|C)[0-9]|^IGH[ADEGM][0-9]?$|^IGKC$|^IGLC[0-9]$"
symbolOf   <- geneAnno$symbol[match(rownames(rawCounts), geneAnno$ensgene)]
keepGene   <- !is.na(symbolOf) & symbolOf != "" & !str_detect(symbolOf, IG_PATTERN)
countsSym  <- rowsum(rawCounts[keepGene, ], group = symbolOf[keepGene])
```

```{r pool}
## Per-isotype donor inclusion, then pool. Cells are ordered by donor so that the
## random-effect grouping is contiguous, and by isotype within donor so the
## design matrix is easy to inspect.
keepByIso <- lapply(setNames(DE_ISOTYPES, DE_ISOTYPES), function(iso)
  cells %>% dplyr::filter(isotype == iso) %>%
    dplyr::count(donorId, name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n >= MIN_CELLS) %>% dplyr::pull(donorId))

pooled <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(DE_ISOTYPES, function(iso)
  cells %>% dplyr::filter(isotype == iso, donorId %in% keepByIso[[iso]]))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(donorId, isotype) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(studyGroup         = factor(studyGroup, levels = c("TC", "DS")),
                isotype            = factor(isotype, levels = DE_ISOTYPES),
                TimeElapsed_binary = factor(TimeElapsed_binary),
                donorId            = factor(donorId))

counts  <- countsSym[, pooled$libid]
libsize <- colSums(counts)
detect  <- rowMeans(counts > 0)
counts  <- counts[detect >= CELL_DETECT, , drop = FALSE]

cat(sprintf("pooled: %d cells, %d donors, %d genes tested\n",
            nrow(pooled), dplyr::n_distinct(pooled$donorId), nrow(counts)))
print(table(studyGroup = pooled$studyGroup, isotype = pooled$isotype))
```

## Which donors contribute which isotypes

The interaction is informed by donors who contribute **both** isotypes; a donor
with only one contributes to the main effects alone. That split is worth seeing
before the models are fitted.

```{r donor_table}
donorTab <- pooled %>%
  dplyr::count(donorId, project, studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary, isotype, name = "nCells") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = isotype, values_from = nCells, values_fill = 0L) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(bothIsotypes = IGHG > 0 & IGHM > 0) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(studyGroup, project)
kable(donorTab, caption = sprintf("Cells per donor per isotype (>= %d to contribute)", MIN_CELLS))
saveSource(donorTab, "Step4_mastComb_donor_table", "one row per donor")

cat(sprintf("\ndonors contributing both isotypes: %d of %d\n",
            sum(donorTab$bothIsotypes), nrow(donorTab)))
if (any(!donorTab$bothIsotypes))
  cat(sprintf("single-isotype donors (main effects only): %s\n",
              paste(donorTab$project[!donorTab$bothIsotypes], collapse = ", ")))

## Full rank is not optional here: with group nested in donor and isotype crossed
## with it, a thin cell can make the interaction inestimable.
dm <- model.matrix(~ TimeElapsed_binary + studyGroup * isotype, data = pooled)
cat(sprintf("\ndesign rank %d of %d columns\n", qr(dm)$rank, ncol(dm)))
print(colnames(dm))
stopifnot(qr(dm)$rank == ncol(dm))
```

# Fit both models

```{r fit_functions}
## MAST reports coefficients in the units of the assay it is handed. The assay
## here is log2(CPM+1), so the coefficients are already log2 -- verified in
## P635_step4_DE_mast.Rmd by fitting the same genes on log2 and natural-log
## assays and recovering a ratio of exactly log(2). No conversion is applied.
makeSCA <- function(cellsDf, cnt, lib, genes = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(genes)) cnt <- cnt[genes, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(cellsDf$libid), colnames(cnt)))
  ex   <- log2(t(t(cnt) / lib) * 1e6 + 1)
  cdat <- data.frame(wellKey = colnames(ex), cellsDf, row.names = colnames(ex))
  fdat <- data.frame(primerid = rownames(ex), row.names = rownames(ex))
  sca  <- MAST::FromMatrix(ex, cData = cdat, fData = fdat, check_sanity = FALSE)
  cdr  <- colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(sca) > 0)
  SummarizedExperiment::colData(sca)$cngeneson <- scale(cdr)[, 1]
  sca
}

## Returns one row per gene per requested coefficient: the hurdle LRT p-value and
## the continuous-component log2 fold change.
runMast <- function(form, coefs, cellsDf = pooled, cnt = counts, lib = libsize) {
  sca <- makeSCA(cellsDf, cnt, lib)
  zz  <- suppressMessages(MAST::zlm(form, sca, method = "glmer", ebayes = FALSE,
                                    strictConvergence = FALSE, parallel = TRUE, silent = TRUE))
  ss  <- suppressMessages(MAST::summary(zz, doLRT = coefs, parallel = TRUE))
  sdt <- as.data.frame(ss$datatable)
  conv <- as.data.frame(zz@converged) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    dplyr::rename(convergedC = C, convergedD = D)

  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(coefs, function(cf) {
    hurdle <- sdt %>% dplyr::filter(contrast == cf, component == "H") %>%
      dplyr::select(gene = primerid, p = `Pr(>Chisq)`)
    lfc <- sdt %>% dplyr::filter(contrast == cf, component == "logFC") %>%
      dplyr::select(gene = primerid, log2FC = coef, ci.lo, ci.hi)
    dplyr::full_join(hurdle, lfc, by = "gene") %>% dplyr::mutate(coefficient = cf)
  })) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(conv, by = "gene") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(converged = convergedC & convergedD)
}

## BH over genes, within a coefficient, restricted to genes that actually fitted.
addFDR <- function(df) df %>% dplyr::group_by(coefficient) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(padj = ifelse(converged & !is.na(p), p, NA_real_),
                padj = p.adjust(padj, method = "BH")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r fit}
fitKey <- list(MIN_CELLS = MIN_CELLS, CELL_DETECT = CELL_DETECT, SEED = SEED,
               nCells = nrow(pooled), nGenes = nrow(counts),
               add = deparse(FORMULA_ADD), int = deparse(FORMULA_INT))

resAdd <- cached("step4_mastComb_additive", fitKey,
                 runMast(FORMULA_ADD, c(COEF_GROUP, "isotypeIGHM"))) %>% addFDR()
resInt <- cached("step4_mastComb_interaction", fitKey,
                 runMast(FORMULA_INT, c(COEF_GROUP, COEF_INT))) %>% addFDR()

chrOf <- geneAnno %>% dplyr::distinct(symbol, chr) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(symbol) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>% dplyr::ungroup()
annot <- function(d) d %>% dplyr::left_join(chrOf, by = c("gene" = "symbol")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(significant = !is.na(padj) & padj < FDR & abs(log2FC) > LFC_MIN,
                chr21 = !is.na(chr) & chr == "21")
resAdd <- annot(resAdd); resInt <- annot(resInt)

saveSource(resAdd, "Step4_mastComb_additive", "one row per gene x coefficient, additive model")
saveSource(resInt, "Step4_mastComb_interaction", "one row per gene x coefficient, interaction model")
```

```{r fit_summary}
fitSummary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  resAdd %>% dplyr::mutate(model = "additive"),
  resInt %>% dplyr::mutate(model = "interaction")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model, coefficient) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nGenes = dplyr::n(), nConverged = sum(converged),
                   nTested = sum(!is.na(padj)),
                   nSig = sum(significant),
                   minPadj = signif(min(padj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
                   medAbsLfc = round(median(abs(log2FC), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                   .groups = "drop")
kable(fitSummary, caption = sprintf("Both models (FDR < %.2f and |log2FC| > %g)", FDR, LFC_MIN))
saveSource(fitSummary, "Step4_mastComb_summary", "one row per model x coefficient")
```

# Is there evidence of an interaction?

```{r interaction_evidence}
intOnly <- resInt %>% dplyr::filter(coefficient == COEF_INT, !is.na(padj))

evid <- tibble::tibble(
  nTested         = nrow(intOnly),
  nSig_FDR        = sum(intOnly$padj < FDR),
  nSig_FDR_and_LFC = sum(intOnly$significant),
  minPadj         = signif(min(intOnly$padj), 3),
  nP_under_05     = sum(intOnly$p < 0.05),
  expectedP_under_05 = round(0.05 * nrow(intOnly)),
  ratio_obs_exp   = round(sum(intOnly$p < 0.05) / (0.05 * nrow(intOnly)), 2))
kable(evid, caption = "Interaction term: observed against the uniform expectation")
saveSource(evid, "Step4_mastComb_interaction_evidence", "one row")
```

The `ratio_obs_exp` column is the quickest read available. Under a true null the
interaction p-values are uniform, so 5% of genes fall below 0.05 by construction
and the ratio is 1. A ratio near 1 with no gene clearing FDR means the additive
model is sufficient for every gene --- the DS effect, such as it is, does not
differ detectably between isotypes.

```{r interaction_hist, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.6}
pHist <- resInt %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(coefficient = factor(coefficient, levels = c(COEF_GROUP, COEF_INT),
                                     labels = c("DS effect (within IgG)",
                                                "interaction: DS effect shift in IgM"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(p)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025, boundary = 0, fill = "grey65", colour = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(intOnly) * 0.025, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ coefficient) +
  labs(x = "hurdle p-value", y = "genes",
       title = "p-value distribution, combined-isotype model",
       subtitle = "dashed line: the flat height expected when nothing is going on") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(pHist)
savePanel(pHist, "Step4_mastComb_pvalue_histogram", width = 7, height = 3.6)
```

```{r interaction_volcano, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5}
d <- intOnly %>% dplyr::mutate(
  direction = dplyr::case_when(!significant ~ "not significant",
                               log2FC > 0 ~ "DS effect larger in IgM",
                               TRUE ~ "DS effect larger in IgG"))
labelled <- d %>% dplyr::slice_min(p, n = N_LABELS, with_ties = FALSE)
pVolc <- ggplot(d, aes(log2FC, -log10(padj), colour = direction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(FDR), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-LFC_MIN, LFC_MIN), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text_repel(data = labelled, aes(label = gene), size = 2.8, colour = "black",
                  max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.3, segment.size = 0.2,
                  show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("DS effect larger in IgM" = "firebrick",
                                 "DS effect larger in IgG" = "steelblue",
                                 "not significant" = "grey75")) +
  labs(x = expression("interaction coefficient (" * log[2] * " scale)"),
       y = expression(-log[10] * "(BH-adjusted p)"), colour = NULL,
       title = "Group-by-isotype interaction",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d cells, %d donors, %d genes | %d at FDR < %.2f and |log2FC| > %g",
                          nrow(pooled), dplyr::n_distinct(pooled$donorId),
                          nrow(d), sum(d$significant), FDR, LFC_MIN)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top")
print(pVolc)
savePanel(pVolc, "Step4_mastComb_interaction_volcano", width = 6.5, height = 5)
```

## Permutation null for the interaction test

```{r permutation}
permNull <- NULL
if (RUN_PERM) {
  permNull <- cached("step4_mastComb_permutation", list(fitKey, N_PERM = N_PERM_INT), {
    donors <- pooled %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId, studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary)
    vapply(seq_len(N_PERM_INT), function(k) {
      set.seed(SEED + 7919L * k)
      repeat {
        sh <- donors %>% dplyr::mutate(
          studyGroup = factor(sample(as.character(studyGroup)), levels = c("TC", "DS")))
        pp <- pooled %>% dplyr::select(-studyGroup) %>%
          dplyr::left_join(sh %>% dplyr::select(donorId, studyGroup), by = "donorId")
        dmp <- model.matrix(~ TimeElapsed_binary + studyGroup * isotype, data = pp)
        if (qr(dmp)$rank == ncol(dmp)) break
      }
      r <- runMast(FORMULA_INT, COEF_INT, cellsDf = pp) %>% addFDR() %>% annot()
      sum(r$significant)
    }, numeric(1))
  })

  permSummary <- tibble::tibble(
    nPermutations = length(permNull),
    observed      = sum(intOnly$significant),
    nullMedian    = median(permNull), nullMax = max(permNull),
    empiricalP    = (1 + sum(permNull >= sum(intOnly$significant))) / (length(permNull) + 1))
  kable(permSummary, caption = "Interaction genes called under permuted group labels")
  saveSource(tibble::tibble(permutation = seq_along(permNull), nSig = permNull),
             "Step4_mastComb_permutation_null", "one row per permutation")
  saveSource(permSummary, "Step4_mastComb_permutation_summary", "one row")
}
```

## Permutation null for the group effect

The interaction null above says nothing about the DS coefficient, and that
coefficient is the one that calls genes. Every earlier document in this project
found that a gene list which looked convincing on its own sat inside its own
permutation null, so the same test is applied here before anything is believed.
The procedure is identical --- shuffle group labels between donors, every cell
carries its donor's new label --- and the statistic is the number of genes the
**additive** model calls.

```{r permutation_group}
permGroup <- NULL
if (RUN_PERM) {
  permGroup <- cached("step4_mastComb_permutation_group", list(fitKey, N_PERM = N_PERM_GROUP), {
    donors <- pooled %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId, studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary)
    vapply(seq_len(N_PERM_GROUP), function(k) {
      set.seed(SEED + 104729L * k)
      repeat {
        sh <- donors %>% dplyr::mutate(
          studyGroup = factor(sample(as.character(studyGroup)), levels = c("TC", "DS")))
        pp <- pooled %>% dplyr::select(-studyGroup) %>%
          dplyr::left_join(sh %>% dplyr::select(donorId, studyGroup), by = "donorId")
        dmp <- model.matrix(~ TimeElapsed_binary + studyGroup + isotype, data = pp)
        if (qr(dmp)$rank == ncol(dmp)) break
      }
      r <- runMast(FORMULA_ADD, COEF_GROUP, cellsDf = pp) %>% addFDR() %>% annot()
      sum(r$significant)
    }, numeric(1))
  })

  obsGroup <- sum(resAdd$significant[resAdd$coefficient == COEF_GROUP])
  permGroupSummary <- tibble::tibble(
    nPermutations = length(permGroup), observed = obsGroup,
    nullMedian = median(permGroup), nullQ90 = quantile(permGroup, 0.9),
    nullMax = max(permGroup),
    empiricalP = (1 + sum(permGroup >= obsGroup)) / (length(permGroup) + 1))
  kable(permGroupSummary,
        caption = "Additive model: genes called under permuted group labels")
  saveSource(tibble::tibble(permutation = seq_along(permGroup), nSig = permGroup),
             "Step4_mastComb_permutation_group_null", "one row per permutation")
  saveSource(permGroupSummary, "Step4_mastComb_permutation_group_summary", "one row")
}
```

```{r permutation_group_plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.4, eval=RUN_PERM}
pPermG <- ggplot(tibble::tibble(nSig = permGroup), aes(nSig)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  geom_point(aes(y = -0.4), shape = 124, size = 2.6, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = permGroupSummary$observed, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = function(l) seq(0, ceiling(l[2]), by = 1)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("genes called at FDR < %.2f and |log2FC| > %g", FDR, LFC_MIN),
       y = "permutations",
       title = "Additive model: permuted group labels versus the observed result",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d permutations; red line = observed (%d). Null median %g, max %g, empirical p = %.3f",
                          length(permGroup), permGroupSummary$observed,
                          permGroupSummary$nullMedian, permGroupSummary$nullMax,
                          permGroupSummary$empiricalP)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8))
print(pPermG)
savePanel(pPermG, "Step4_mastComb_permutation_group", width = 6.5, height = 3.4)
```

# Does the combined model agree with the separate ones?

If the additive model is a fair summary, its single DS coefficient should sit
between the two per-isotype coefficients estimated independently, and should
correlate with both.

```{r compare_separate}
sepFiles <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figure_source_data", "mast",
                      sprintf("Step4_mast_DE_%s.csv", DE_ISOTYPES))
if (all(file.exists(sepFiles))) {
  sep <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(DE_ISOTYPES), function(i)
    readr::read_csv(sepFiles[i], show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(gene, isotype = DE_ISOTYPES[i], lfc_sep = log2FC, p_sep = p)))
  addG <- resAdd %>% dplyr::filter(coefficient == COEF_GROUP) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, lfc_add = log2FC)

  cmp <- sep %>% dplyr::inner_join(addG, by = "gene") %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(lfc_sep), !is.na(lfc_add))
  cmpStats <- cmp %>% dplyr::group_by(isotype) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(nGenes = dplyr::n(),
                     pearson = round(cor(lfc_sep, lfc_add), 3),
                     spearman = round(cor(lfc_sep, lfc_add, method = "spearman"), 3),
                     .groups = "drop")
  kable(cmpStats, caption = "Additive combined DS effect versus the separately-fitted per-isotype effects")
  saveSource(cmpStats, "Step4_mastComb_vs_separate", "one row per isotype")

  pCmp <- ggplot(cmp, aes(lfc_sep, lfc_add)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey88") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey88") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.35, colour = "#3E5C8A") +
    facet_wrap(~ isotype, labeller = labeller(isotype = c(IGHG = "IgG", IGHM = "IgM"))) +
    labs(x = expression("separate per-isotype model: " * log[2] * " fold change"),
         y = expression("combined additive model: " * log[2] * " fold change"),
         title = "One pooled DS effect against two separately-fitted ones") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  print(pCmp)
  savePanel(pCmp, "Step4_mastComb_vs_separate", width = 7, height = 4)
} else {
  cat("per-isotype MAST results not found; skipping the comparison\n")
}
```

# The additive DS effect

The additive model estimates **one** DS effect per gene, shared across isotypes
by construction, so there is nothing to plot it against: the natural pair is a
volcano and a heatmap of what it called.

Chromosome 21 is carried by **shape**, not colour. Five of the seven called genes
are themselves chr21, so a second colour layer for chr21 would simply be painted
over by the "called" layer and the overlap would be invisible.

```{r additive_volcano, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6}
addDS <- resAdd %>% dplyr::filter(coefficient == COEF_GROUP, !is.na(padj), !is.na(log2FC))
## A couple of genes return a hurdle p but no continuous estimate; they cannot be
## placed on a fold-change axis, so they are dropped explicitly rather than being
## discarded by ggplot with a warning.
nDropped <- sum(resAdd$coefficient == COEF_GROUP & !is.na(resAdd$padj) & is.na(resAdd$log2FC))
saveSource(addDS, "Step4_mastComb_additive_DS_effect", "one row per gene, additive DS effect")
cat(sprintf("%d genes on the volcano; %d called (%d chr21); %d dropped for want of a continuous estimate\n",
            nrow(addDS), sum(addDS$significant), sum(addDS$significant & addDS$chr21), nDropped))
cat("  (these counts were previously the figure subtitle; the panel is now bare for the manuscript)\n")

calledLab <- sprintf("called (FDR < %.2f, |log2FC| > %g)", FDR, LFC_MIN)
## One categorical variable drives both shape and fill, so the two scales merge
## into a single four-key legend. Mapping chr21 to shape and significance to
## fill separately produced two legends that the reader had to combine mentally.
## "chr21" rather than "chromosome 21", matching the heatmap row labels. Short
## enough now that the two-line wrapping is no longer needed.
LV <- c("DE, chr21", "DE, non-chr21", "not DE, chr21", "not DE, non-chr21")
addDS <- addDS %>% dplyr::mutate(grp = factor(dplyr::case_when(
   significant &  chr21 ~ LV[1],
   significant & !chr21 ~ LV[2],
  !significant &  chr21 ~ LV[3],
  TRUE                  ~ LV[4]), levels = LV))

## The called genes, plus SON. SON is not called -- its log2 fold change of 0.93
## sits just under the cutoff -- but it carries the smallest adjusted p-value in
## the analysis by a factor of fifty, and it is a chromosome 21 gene, so leaving
## the highest point on the plot anonymous would be the more misleading choice.
## Picked by rank, not by name, so it survives a re-run that shifts the numbers.
labV <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  addDS %>% dplyr::filter(significant),
  addDS %>% dplyr::filter(!significant) %>% dplyr::slice_min(padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
) %>% dplyr::distinct()
xl <- max(abs(addDS$log2FC))

## Identical name, breaks and guide in both scales: that is what makes ggplot
## merge them rather than draw two legends. Layers stay separate for draw order.
keyGuide <- guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.4))

pVolc2 <- ggplot(addDS, aes(log2FC, -log10(padj))) +
  ## Solid lines mark the origin, dashed lines the calling thresholds; drawn
  ## first so both sit behind the points.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(FDR), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-LFC_MIN, LFC_MIN), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, grp == LV[4]),
             aes(shape = grp, fill = grp), colour = "grey85", size = 1.2, stroke = 0, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, grp == LV[3]),
             aes(shape = grp, fill = grp), colour = "white", size = 2.7, stroke = 0.35) +
  geom_point(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, significant),
             aes(shape = grp, fill = grp), colour = "white", size = 3.6, stroke = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = labV, aes(label = gene, fontface = ifelse(chr21, "bold", "plain")),
                  size = 2.9, colour = "grey15", max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.45,
                  segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey60", min.segment.length = 0) +
  ## Both scales must carry identical name, breaks and limits, or ggplot draws
  ## two legends instead of merging them into one.
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, breaks = LV, limits = LV, drop = FALSE,
                     values = setNames(c(22, 21, 22, 21), LV),
                     guide = keyGuide) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, breaks = LV, limits = LV, drop = FALSE,
                    values = setNames(c("#B2182B", "#B2182B", "#2166ac", "grey85"), LV),
                    guide = keyGuide) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-xl, xl)) +
  ## "FDR" rather than "BH-adjusted p": they are the same quantity, and every
  ## threshold in this project is quoted as an FDR, so the axis should match.
  labs(x = expression(log[2] * " fold change, DS vs Ctrl"),
       y = expression(-log[10] * "(FDR)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5),
        legend.key.spacing.y = unit(3, "pt"))

print(pVolc2)
savePanel(pVolc2, "Step4_mastComb_additive_volcano", width = 7, height = 5.6)
```

## The called genes, donor by donor

Both isotypes appear here. That is not a breakout of the estimate --- the model
has only one --- it is the check on the assumption behind it. If the DS effect
really is shared, each gene should shift the same way in the IgG block and the
IgM block.

```{r additive_heatmap, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=3.8}
calledG <- addDS %>% dplyr::filter(significant) %>% dplyr::arrange(padj)
if (nrow(calledG)) {
  cpmC <- log2(t(t(counts[calledG$gene, , drop = FALSE]) / libsize) * 1e6 + 1)
  hLong <- as.data.frame(as.table(cpmC)) %>%
    stats::setNames(c("gene", "libid", "log2CPM")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pooled %>% dplyr::select(libid, project, studyGroup, isotype), by = "libid") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene, project, studyGroup, isotype) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(log2CPM = mean(log2CPM), nCells = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene) %>% dplyr::mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(log2CPM))) %>% dplyr::ungroup()
  saveSource(hLong, "Step4_mastComb_additive_heatmap", "one row per gene x donor x isotype")

  ordP <- pooled %>% dplyr::distinct(project, studyGroup) %>% dplyr::arrange(studyGroup, project)
  geneOrd <- calledG %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(chr21), padj) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(lab = ifelse(chr21, paste0(gene, "  (chr21)"), gene))
  ## Display labels only: "TC" is the internal study-group code and "IGHG"/"IGHM"
  ## the internal isotype codes. The data, the source csv and every model keep
  ## the original values; only the strips change.
  hLong <- hLong %>% dplyr::mutate(
    project    = factor(project, levels = ordP$project),
    gene       = factor(gene, levels = rev(geneOrd$gene)),
    studyGroup = factor(ifelse(studyGroup == "TC", "Ctrl", "DS"), levels = c("Ctrl", "DS")),
    isotype    = factor(ifelse(isotype == "IGHG", "IgG", "IgM"), levels = c("IgG", "IgM")))
  limZ <- max(abs(hLong$z), na.rm = TRUE)

  pHeat <- ggplot(hLong, aes(project, gene, fill = z)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(studyGroup, isotype), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0,
                         limits = c(-limZ, limZ), name = "row z-score\nof log2(CPM+1)") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = setNames(geneOrd$lab, geneOrd$gene)) +
    ## Bare for the composite: the gene count and the centring both belong in the
    ## figure legend, not repeated on every panel.
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    ## Donor identifiers removed: the facet strips already say which group and
    ## isotype each column belongs to, and the individual IDs are not readable at
    ## supplemental size. They remain in the source csv.
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), panel.grid = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))
  print(pHeat)
  savePanel(pHeat, "Step4_mastComb_additive_heatmap", width = 8.5, height = 3.8)

  dirChk <- hLong %>% dplyr::group_by(gene, isotype, studyGroup) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = mean(log2CPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = studyGroup, values_from = m) %>%
    ## Ctrl, not TC: the strips were relabelled above and pivot_wider names the
    ## column from the displayed value.
    dplyr::mutate(shift = DS - Ctrl) %>% dplyr::select(gene, isotype, shift) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = isotype, values_from = shift) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sameDirection = sign(IgG) == sign(IgM))
  print(kable(dirChk %>% dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(IgG, IgM), ~ round(.x, 2))),
              caption = "Shift in donor-mean log2(CPM+1), DS minus Ctrl, within each isotype"))
  saveSource(dirChk, "Step4_mastComb_additive_direction_check", "one row per called gene")
  cat(sprintf("\n%d of %d called genes shift the same way in both isotypes.\n",
              sum(dirChk$sameDirection), nrow(dirChk)))
} else cat("no gene called; nothing to draw\n")
```

# Gene set enrichment (cameraPR)

Significance comes from `limma::cameraPR`, which corrects for inter-gene
correlation, matching every other step-4 document. `fgsea` is deliberately not
used: its null resamples genes as though they were independent, and on this
dataset several sets clear fgsea FDR < 0.05 while none survives the correlation
adjustment.

Two statistics are tested: the pooled DS effect from the additive model, and the
interaction term. Per-isotype enrichment is already in
`P635_step4_DE_mast.Rmd` and is not repeated here.

```{r gsea, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5}
hallmark <- tryCatch(msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = GSEA_COLLECTION),
                     error = function(e) msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",
                                                          category = GSEA_COLLECTION))
pathways <- split(hallmark$gene_symbol, hallmark$gs_name)

## The additive DS effect only. The interaction term has no gene-level signal to
## enrich, and a second panel invites the figure to be read as an isotype
## breakout, which the additive model does not provide.
camIn <- list("DS effect (pooled, additive model)" =
                resAdd %>% dplyr::filter(coefficient == COEF_GROUP))
cam <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(camIn), function(ef) {
  d <- camIn[[ef]] %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), !is.na(p), !is.na(log2FC))
  s <- sign(d$log2FC) * -log10(d$p); names(s) <- d$gene; s <- s[is.finite(s)]
  idx <- limma::ids2indices(pathways, names(s))
  idx <- idx[lengths(idx) >= GSEA_MIN_SIZE & lengths(idx) <= GSEA_MAX_SIZE]
  cm <- limma::cameraPR(s, idx, sort = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(effect = ef, pathwayShort = sub("^HALLMARK_", "", rownames(cm)),
                 nGenesInSet = cm$NGenes, direction = cm$Direction,
                 cameraP = cm$PValue, cameraFDR = cm$FDR)
}))
saveSource(cam, "Step4_mastComb_GSEA_cameraPR", "one row per statistic x pathway")

camSig <- cam %>% dplyr::filter(cameraFDR < GSEA_FDR) %>% dplyr::arrange(effect, cameraP)
if (nrow(camSig)) {
  kable(camSig %>% dplyr::transmute(effect, pathway = pathwayShort, direction,
                                    cameraP = signif(cameraP, 3), cameraFDR = signif(cameraFDR, 3)),
        caption = sprintf("Hallmark sets at cameraPR FDR < %.2f", GSEA_FDR))
} else cat(sprintf("no hallmark set reaches cameraPR FDR < %.2f for either statistic\n", GSEA_FDR))

kable(cam %>% dplyr::arrange(cameraP) %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) %>%
        dplyr::transmute(effect, pathway = pathwayShort, direction,
                         cameraP = signif(cameraP, 2), cameraFDR = signif(cameraFDR, 2), nGenesInSet),
      caption = "Ten smallest cameraPR p-values across both statistics")

highlight <- union(
  cam %>% dplyr::group_by(pathwayShort) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(bestP = min(cameraP), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::slice_min(bestP, n = GSEA_N_SHOW, with_ties = FALSE) %>% dplyr::pull(pathwayShort),
  camSig$pathwayShort) %>% unique()
## The axis is the FDR, not the raw p, so that bar length and bar colour encode
## the same quantity: a bar crosses the dashed line exactly when it is coloured
## as significant. Plotting -log10(p) against an FDR-based colour let a long bar
## sit next to a "n.s." label with nothing on the figure to explain the gap.
pGsea <- cam %>% dplyr::filter(pathwayShort %in% highlight) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(signedLogFDR = ifelse(direction == "Up", 1, -1) * -log10(cameraFDR)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(signedLogFDR, reorder(pathwayShort, signedLogFDR),
             fill = cameraFDR < GSEA_FDR)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1) * -log10(GSEA_FDR), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey75"),
                    labels = c(`TRUE` = sprintf("cameraPR FDR < %.2f", GSEA_FDR),
                               `FALSE` = "n.s."), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = bquote("signed " * -log[10] * "(cameraPR FDR)   (positive: up in DS; dashed: FDR " * .(GSEA_FDR) * ")"),
       y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ## A one-entry legend reading "n.s." carries no information the dashed
  ## threshold does not already give. Made conditional rather than deleted, so a
  ## re-run that does find something still labels it.
  theme(legend.position = if (nrow(camSig)) "right" else "none")
print(pGsea)
savePanel(pGsea, "Step4_mastComb_GSEA_cameraPR", width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

# Supplemental figure

The three panels of the combined-isotype analysis assembled into one figure:
**A** the DS effect from the additive model, **B** the genes it called shown
donor by donor, **C** hallmark enrichment of the same ranking.

One column, A over B over C. Panel titles and subtitles are stripped from all
three: in a composite that text belongs in the figure legend, and leaving it on
some panels but not others reads as an oversight.

```{r supplemental_figure, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=12.1}
haveAll <- all(vapply(c("pVolc2", "pHeat", "pGsea"), exists, logical(1)))
if (haveAll) {
  ## Heights, not equal thirds: the heatmap is only seven rows deep and the
  ## volcano needs the most vertical room for its labels.
  ## free(type = "label", side = "l") exempts the volcano's y-axis title from the
  ## left-edge alignment. Without it patchwork widens the axis-text column to fit
  ## B's gene names and C's pathway names, and A's short "0 1 2 3" leaves its
  ## title stranded at the far left. No vjust or margin can close that gap --
  ## the title and the axis text sit in different grid columns.
  ## Legend text is built from the figures themselves so it cannot drift out of
  ## step with the panels; strwrap does the line breaking, since a patchwork
  ## caption does not wrap on its own.
  nBoth <- sum(donorTab$bothIsotypes)
  capTxt <- sprintf(paste(
    "Supplemental Figure. Differential expression between DS and Ctrl in spike-specific B cells,",
    "modelled across both isotypes at once (MAST, donor random effect).",
    "%d cells from %d donors (%d IgG, %d IgM; %d donors contributed both isotypes).",
    "(A) Volcano of the %s genes tested; %d called at FDR < %.2f and |log2FC| > %g, %d of them on chr21.",
    "SON is labelled although its fold change falls just below the cutoff.",
    "(B) Donor means per isotype for the called genes; rows centred and scaled.",
    "(C) Hallmark gene sets ranked by cameraPR. Dashed lines mark FDR %.2f throughout."),
    nrow(pooled), dplyr::n_distinct(pooled$donorId),
    sum(pooled$isotype == "IGHG"), sum(pooled$isotype == "IGHM"), nBoth,
    format(nrow(addDS), big.mark = ","), sum(addDS$significant), FDR, LFC_MIN,
    sum(addDS$significant & addDS$chr21), FDR)
  capTxt <- paste(strwrap(capTxt, width = 112), collapse = "\n")

  suppFig <- patchwork::free(pVolc2, type = "label", side = "l") / pHeat / pGsea +
    patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.62, 0.88)) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      tag_levels = "A", caption = capTxt,
      theme = ggplot2::theme(
        plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8.2, lineheight = 1.3,
                                             margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)))) &
    ggplot2::theme(plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
  print(suppFig)
  savePanel(suppFig, "SupplFig_mastComb_ABC", width = 8.5, height = 12.1)
  cat("\n--- legend as placed on the figure ---\n"); cat(capTxt, "\n")
  cat("wrote SupplFig_mastComb_ABC (A volcano, B heatmap, C hallmark GSEA)\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("missing panel object(s): %s -- supplemental figure not assembled\n",
              paste(setdiff(c("pVolc2", "pHeat", "pGsea"),
                            Filter(exists, c("pVolc2", "pHeat", "pGsea"))), collapse = ", ")))
}
```

# What this shows

```{r bottom_line, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
nSigInt <- sum(intOnly$significant)
permTxt <- if (RUN_PERM && !is.null(permNull))
  sprintf(" Under %d permutations of the group labels the same test called a median of %g genes (max %g), so the observed count is%s what label shuffling produces.",
          length(permNull), median(permNull), max(permNull),
          if (nSigInt > max(permNull)) " above" else " indistinguishable from") else ""

cat(sprintf("
1. **The interaction test finds %d gene%s.** Of %d genes tested, %d fall below p = 0.05
   against %d expected by chance (ratio %.2f), and the smallest adjusted p-value is %s.%s

2. **The additive model is therefore sufficient.** Constraining the DS effect to be the
   same in IgG and IgM costs nothing in fit for any gene, which is the formal version of
   what the concordance scatterplots showed descriptively.

3. **This does not mean the isotypes are biologically identical.** It means that at
   %d cells from %d donors, with no gene-level DS signal in either isotype to begin with,
   there is no difference between two effects that are both indistinguishable from zero.
   A test for a difference between two nulls is not informative about biology.
",
nSigInt, if (nSigInt == 1) "" else "s", nrow(intOnly),
sum(intOnly$p < 0.05), round(0.05 * nrow(intOnly)),
sum(intOnly$p < 0.05) / (0.05 * nrow(intOnly)),
format(signif(min(intOnly$padj), 3)), permTxt,
nrow(pooled), dplyr::n_distinct(pooled$donorId)))
```

```{r save}
step4comb <- list(additive = resAdd, interaction = resInt, pooled = pooled,
                  donorTable = donorTab, evidence = evid, permutation = permNull, permutationGroup = permGroup,
                  params = list(MIN_CELLS = MIN_CELLS, CELL_DETECT = CELL_DETECT,
                                formulaAdd = deparse(FORMULA_ADD),
                                formulaInt = deparse(FORMULA_INT),
                                FDR = FDR, LFC_MIN = LFC_MIN, N_PERM_INT = N_PERM_INT, N_PERM_GROUP = N_PERM_GROUP, SEED = SEED),
                  sessionInfo = sessionInfo())
saveRDS(step4comb, file.path(OUT_DIR, "step4_differential_expression_mast_combined.rds"))
cat(sprintf("wrote %s\n", file.path(OUT_DIR, "step4_differential_expression_mast_combined.rds")))
```
